title: Promote with enough power
objective: Move your pawn to the far edge. Choose a piece that can help you win.

commentary_source.name: Uroschess original synthetic lesson
commentary_source.attribution: Original instructional text and synthetic endgame position

steps.explanation: The white king protects the pawn, and Black's king is too far away. Push the pawn, then choose the promotion piece carefully.
steps.detail: A queen is usually the simplest choice. A rook can also force checkmate. A lone bishop or knight cannot checkmate a bare king.

question.prompt: Push the pawn. At the far edge, choose a piece that can help you win.
hints: Move the pawn from e6 to e7.
On e8, choose a queen or rook.

tree.feedback: Good. The pawn is one step from promotion.

children.feedback: Black's king moves, but it cannot catch the pawn.
e8=Q gives White a queen. White now has enough material to force checkmate.
e8=R works too. A king and rook can force checkmate.
A lone bishop cannot force checkmate against a bare king. Choose more power.
A lone knight cannot force checkmate against a bare king. Choose more power.
Black tries another square, but promotion is still safe.
e8=Q keeps a decisive material advantage.
e8=R also leaves enough material to force mate.

question.other_legal_move_text: That move may be legal, but the safe passed pawn is ready to advance now.

takeaway: When your pawn is safe, push it to the far edge. A queen is the easiest choice. A rook can win too.
